chapter_mission: Aftermath on Veranthos. Veraine in containment, composed, already writing equations; defeated by results, unbroken by conversion. Torin diminished; Sera chooses to stay. Kael departs freely — the ability to leave is the proof that this was different. Ben and Desh laugh.
chapter_turn: Every character's ending is chosen. The book's argument — that choosing differently than the predecessors is the answer — lands in the shape of these resolutions: Veraine's refusal, Sera's presence, Kael's departure, Desh's laughter. None of them is forced. None is denied.

scene_plan.purpose: Ben at Veraine's containment. She sits cross-legged in Sera's Force-lock field, already writing equations in the dust with one finger. Composed. Academic. Genuinely curious about the emergent pattern they produced. 'The emergence you produced was interesting. I will think about it.' Not concession. Not conversion. Ben learns the texture of intellectual enemies: they are not convinced by arguments, only by results they cannot dismiss, and even then they adapt the theory rather than abandon it. Ben leaves. She keeps writing.

Ridgeline above the new seal's hum. Torin on the edge, posture unchanged, presence diminished. Warmth muted, humor gone quiet, Force-presence lighter in a way that should be freeing and is devastating. Sera walks up, sits beside him without speaking. After a long time, his hand finds hers. Lighter grip than before. It's there. Ben watches from a distance and understands he is watching love without control — Sera's arc resolved in its final word, chosen presence.

Camp, morning. Kael has his bag packed before anyone wakes. Everything he owns slung over one shoulder. He finds Ben at the ship and they shake hands — firm, brief, the most Kael gesture possible. He turns toward his transport without looking back. Desh says something that shouldn't be funny. Ben laughs. Desh laughs. The sound carries up the ridge where Sera and Torin sit; for a moment, Torin's eyes crinkle. The laugh between equals. The resolution the GAG pattern needed and never got.

relationship_turns.to: permanent question — Veraine in containment is the book's answer to the villainy question: some people are not convertible, only contained. Her equations in the dust are the book's unresolved counterpoint. She will spend years rationalising; she may produce something important. The book does not tell us which
chosen presence — Sera's arc resolved in a hand on his hand on a ridgeline. She is not fixing him. She is with him. The thousand-year wound has produced something like peace, imperfect and earned

freely departed — the ability to leave is the proof the story was different. Kael does not reject the group; he exercises the freedom the book's argument demanded he be offered. His arc resolves as the absence his body makes when he walks away
equals — the laugh is the GAG wound's scar tissue finally forming. Not forgotten; healed enough to produce sound that is not grief

relationship_turns.from: first anchor taken (Ch 26 s3, per D2)
relationship_turns.to: departing anchor — Ben leaves Veranthos with the tether in his perception. The commitment is priced; the price is that he will return, and the return is no longer a burden but a rhythm. The priced commitment now has shape in the chapter's closing register

exit_vector: Kael's transport lifting from the camp. Sera and Torin small on the ridgeline. Veraine's containment visible in the middle distance with the guard posted. The Steady Returns on the pad, Desh already running pre-flight. Ben at the ramp, the first-anchor tether (per Ch 26 D2) registered in his perception as a continuous presence — the seal he is leaving but not leaving permanently; the renewal he will return to. The laugh still in the air. One scene left in the book, and it is on Coruscant.
notes: The chapter's register is falling action and chosen ending, not triumph. Veraine's scene in s1 is the book's final philosophical note — her refusal to concede is the book's honest answer to 'what do you do about people you cannot convert.' Her equations in the dust are the image that lingers. The Sera/Torin scene in s2 is the book's emotional climax after the plot climax; understated grip of hands on hand, no dialogue, no articulation of what she is doing there. The closing laugh between Ben and Desh is the Allston register of the whole book's Allston register — earned joy, small, offered to a reader who has followed these two for 27 chapters. Voice: Zahn-quiet in s1 (Veraine's composure sets the register); Stover-permitted density for s2 but under half the scene in interiority (the ridgeline, the hand, the small grip anchor the body); Allston-warmth for s3 with the laugh as the exit line. Anti-patterns: (a) do not give Veraine a concession or softening in s1 — the refusal is the book's honesty; (b) Sera and Torin do not speak in s2; the hand is the sentence; (c) the laugh in s3 must not be about anything specific — the reader does not need to hear Desh's joke; they hear the laugh.
